pre: Using a dictionary: parts of speech
Discuss everyday life and ask for personal information.
What do you do after school?
I usually spend time with my friends after school.
Imagine you are on a student exchange. Describe similarities and differences between your life there and at home.
Using a dictionary: synonyms and antonyms
Past simple / continuous; while, as, when
Ask for directions, then explain a route.
Could you tell me how to get to the station?
Write a travel blog entry about a place you visited. Describe the journey, the place and what you did.
Invite somebody to eat out and respond to an invitation.
Would you like to have lunch with me?
Write a short invitation or announcement. Make the purpose, place, time and necessary action clear.
An email: description of a room
Phrasal verbs: literal and non-literal meanings
Houses and homes • Parts of a house
Comparatives; as … as; too / enough; verb patterns
Ask permission and describe your room.
What is your favourite room in the house?
Could I use your computer, please?
Write an email describing a room. Organize your description and explain why the room matters to you.
A letter: description of a person
Present perfect / past simple; already / just / yet; for / since
Describe a photo and discuss fears or achievements.
Have you ever tried a risky sport?
I have never tried a risky sport.
Write a letter describing a person you admire. Use paragraphs, topic sentences and linking expressions.
Using a dictionary: verb and noun collocations
School: bad behaviour • School: compound nouns
Will / going to; first / zero conditional; probability
Make an offer or suggestion and respond to it.
How can schools help young people?
Why don't we study together after class?
Write a for and against essay on an education issue. Brainstorm both sides and use expressions of contrast.
Using a dictionary: words with more than one meaning
Must / have to; second conditional; I wish
Ask for advice and give a reason for your suggestion.
What would you do if you started a business?
I think you should ask your teacher for advice.
Write a formal email. Explain the reason for writing, make a clear request and use an appropriate register.
Express and justify an opinion about an achievement.
What do you think is the greatest achievement?
In my opinion, this achievement has changed many lives.
Write an opinion essay. State your view, support it with examples and write a conclusion.
Parts of a newspaper • Film genres
Reported speech; say / tell; question tags
Give news and react to what somebody tells you.
What kind of films do you enjoy?
That sounds interesting. What happened next?
Write a film review. Describe the film without revealing everything, evaluate it and recommend it to a suitable audience.
Persuade somebody, agree or disagree and give reasons.
What is your favourite item of clothing made of?
I agree with you, but we should consider another option.
Describe a process using sequence expressions and suitable passive forms. Check spelling and punctuation.
int: Present simple / continuous; speculation; verb patterns
Speculate about a photo and discuss first impressions.
He looks as if he is enjoying the conversation.
Write an informal email introducing yourself and describing family or friends in a photo. Check grammar, spelling and word order.
Types of holiday • Travel and transport
Persuade a partner to choose a trip and negotiate an agreement.
That sounds interesting, but I would prefer another tour.
Write a story about a memorable journey. Begin in an interesting way, order the events and bring the story to an end.
Past simple / present perfect; perfect simple / continuous
Give news and show your reaction and attitude.
What makes you feel pleased or disappointed?
I have been practising regularly and I feel much better.
Write a personal letter. Show your attitude and explain reasons and purposes using suitable linking expressions.
Ask for an opinion and support your own view with arguments.
What can people do to help a charity?
In my view, volunteering can make a real difference.
Write an opinion essay about an issue discussed in the unit. Organize each argument into a clear paragraph.
Crime and punishment • Law and order
First / second conditional; modals of obligation, prohibition, permission
Make an apology and accept or respond to an apology.
Why can it be difficult to apologize?
I'm sorry about what happened. It won't happen again.
Write a letter to a newspaper about a problem. Make suggestions and explain their possible results.
Compare photos and discuss advertising or spending.
What kinds of advertisements do you see every day?
The advertisement seems to be aimed at young people.
Write a formal letter of complaint. Explain what went wrong, the effect on you and what response you expect.
Using a dictionary: homonyms and homophones
Make a polite complaint and ask somebody to do something.
How would you describe the texture of your favourite food?
Would you mind speaking a little more quietly?
Write a report on survey findings. Use an appropriate structure, approximations and linking expressions.
Third conditional; I wish / if only; past speculation
Give a short presentation about a decision and its consequences.
What important decision have you made?
If I had known about the opportunity, I would have applied.
Write a covering letter for a job. Give specific evidence of your skills and experience instead of general claims.
Defining / non-defining relative clauses; introductory It
Ask for instructions, an explanation or clarification.
Which gadget could you not live without?
Could you explain how to attach a document to an email?
Write a for and against essay about technology. Keep the discussion neutral and consider both sides.
Around the world in one dance
Fixed phrases with two key words
Debate the value of art and respond to another opinion.
What event would you recommend to a friend?
Although I see your point, I think art has an important role.
Write a review of an event. Use precise evaluative adjectives and emphasis, then give a recommendation.
